title: Primitives refactor + ledger migration proposal
body:
Purpose
------
This note proposes a pragmatic refactor for our Terraform primitives that introduces a lightweight output ledger, clearer variable shaping, and a migration plan focused on low-risk canaries for Dedicated and Private deployments (VPC + on-prem). The goal is to make module outputs deterministic across clouds, reduce accidental consumer coupling, and give a repeatable upgrade path with tests and rollback hooks.

Background / motivation
-----------------------
- We have drifting output shapes and many ad-hoc consumers that read provider-specific fields (e.g., gke.cluster_name vs eks.cluster_id) causing brittle upgrades.
- On-prem variants require different surface area (no cloud-assigned subnets, sometimes manual IP allocations).
- Current upgrade experience: ad-hoc, manual, and risky for customers with reserved Dedicated capacity.

High-level proposal
-------------------
1) Introduce an outputs ledger file emitted by modules (terraform output metadata) containing a canonical key set and a small per-cloud adapter map.
2) Converge on a minimal canonical output surface (cluster_endpoint, cluster_ca_pem, control_plane_nodes, network_subnets, service_account_roles) and map provider-specific extras into adapter outputs only consumed by infra-adapters.
3) Add a semver + migration-metadata file for each module (module.meta) that describes breaking changes and automated shim logic.
4) Build a test harness (terraform-integration-tests) that validates ledger shape + consumer smoke tests across EKS/GKE/AKS and a simple on-prem kubeadm cluster simulator.

Implementation details: outputs ledger
----------------------------------
- Each module should emit: outputs_ledger_version (string), outputs_ledger_hash (sha256 of sorted key:value pairs), outputs_canonical_keys (list).
- Ledger file (JSON blob exposed as a terraform output string) example: "{\"version\":\"v1\",\"hash\":\"abc123\",\"canonical\":[\"cluster_endpoint\",\"cluster_ca_pem\"]}".
- Consumers should prefer canonical keys. Provider-specific fields must be placed under outputs_adapters.<provider>.* so changes can be scoped and deprecated independently.

Canonical outputs (initial v1 list)
-----------------------------------
- cluster_id  (string)  -- neutral identifier (module-generated UUID)
- cluster_endpoint (string) -- kube API host
- cluster_ca_pem (string) -- CA cert (PEM)
- control_plane_count (number) -- count of control-plane nodes/VMs
- network_subnets (list) -- CIDR blocks exposed for workloads
- service_account_roles (map) -- role names the platform creates and maintains
- telemetry_signals (map) -- minimal required telemetry hooks (prometheus endpoint / push gateway)

Adapter outputs (examples)
-------------------------
- outputs_adapters.aws.eks_cluster_name
- outputs_adapters.gcp.gke_self_link
- outputs_adapters.azure.aks_resource_group
- outputs_adapters.onprem.node_pool_manifest_path

Variable shaping guidance
------------------------
- Avoid raw provider objects (no aws_subnet.* being surfaced). Use high-level inputs: "control_plane": { "count": 3, "instance_type": "m6i.xlarge" }
- When an on-prem consumer must supply physical constraints, use a single structured variable "deployment_constraints" with optional fields (ip_ranges, vlan_ids, rack_affinity). Keep defaults nil for cloud flows.
- Provide interpolation helpers (documentation + examples) rather than complex computed variables in the module.

Module metadata and versioning
-----------------------------
- module.meta (HCL-friendly key/value file checked into module repo) with fields: semver, ledger_version, breaking_changes list (human text), auto_shim_supported boolean.
- Release process: bump semver for public API changes; bump ledger_version when canonical outputs change. CI validates semantic mapping.

Upgrade & migration plan (overview)
-----------------------------------
1) Inventory: run an automated scan (terraform state reader) to map modules consuming primitive outputs. Produce a dependency graph and consumer count.
2) Patch modules to read from canonical outputs with a fallback to provider-specific adapter keys. Create small compatibility shims where consumer upgrade isn't trivial.
3) Publish modules with new ledger v1 (feature-flagged). Start with internal infra and non-customer Dedicated clusters.
4) Canary: deploy to three target clusters (one hosted Dedicated, one private cloud, one on-prem testbed). Run smoke tests: cluster create, kubeconfig validity, basic workload scheduling, IAM bindings.
5) Monitor for 72 hours with our Console telemetry hooks (token/route-level). If telemetry shows higher error rates or increased rollout latencies, roll back.
6) After successful canary, open a phased migration board for customer migrations with per-customer runbooks.

Rollback strategy
-----------------
- All changes must be reversible in a single terraform apply (we'll use a compatibility toggle variable module.enable_ledger = false).
- Keep a last-known-good outputs_ledger_hash in state and block accidental apply if ledger hash diverges and module.enable_ledger == true unless explicitly forced.

Testing plan
------------
- Unit: validate output names, ledger hash consistency, module.meta present.
- Integration: terraform-integration-tests that runs modules in parallel across providers. Use ephemeral project accounts to avoid long-lived cloud resources.
- Consumer smoke: a lightweight consumer module that reads canonical outputs and performs the minimal operations (create namespace, apply rolebinding, run a pod).
- On-prem: run kubeadm-based emulator in CI (small VMs) that validates kubeconfig + CA chain delivery.

Operational signals to surface
----------------------------
- output_ledger_mismatch_count (how many modules produced unexpected shapes)
- consumer_fallback_count (how often consumer used adapter outputs instead of canonical)
- migration_blockers (list of consumers that cannot auto-migrate)

Example variable + output snippet (illustrative only)
----------------------------------------------------
variable "control_plane" {
  type = object({ count = number, instance_type = string })
  default = { count = 3, instance_type = "standard" }
}

output "outputs_ledger" {
  value = jsonencode({ version = "v1", hash = /* computed */ "", canonical = ["cluster_id","cluster_endpoint"] })
}

output "cluster_endpoint" { value = aws_eks_cluster.cluster.endpoint }
output "outputs_adapters" { value = { aws = { eks_name = aws_eks_cluster.cluster.name } } }

Migration checklist (short)
--------------------------
- [ ] Inventory scan script (owner: Noah) - 2w
- [ ] Design review + signoff (owner: Ravi) - 1w
- [ ] Implement ledger outputs in network + cluster modules (Sofia) - 3w
- [ ] Integration tests + CI (Marcus) - 2w
- [ ] Internal canary + runbook (Infra eng lead) - 1w
- [ ] Customer migration scheduling doc (Customer Success) - ongoing

Open questions / tradeoffs
-------------------------
- How opinionated should the canonical surface be? (minimal vs ergonomics)
- Do we block by default if ledger hash changes? That prevents accidental drift but may be disruptive for automation.
- To what extent do we support auto-shimming vs forcing consumer updates?

Next steps
----------
- Iterate this doc with infra-primitives working group and finalize canonical v1 in two weeks.
- Start the inventory scan and share results in the next Retro.
- Create a prototype module branch that emits outputs_ledger and adapter outputs; add to terraform-integration-tests.

Notes to self
-------------
- Keep examples tiny. Avoid offering provider-specific helpers unless they are behind a provider flag.
- This is intentionally conservative: opt for shim-first, break-later approach.

References
----------
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-primitives/pull/214
- Confluence: Primitives Design Index
